<br>

The SciLifeLab Course Page Template provides the structure and configuration needed to create and publish your course website using Quarto and GitHub Pages.

This chapter will guide you through creating your own course repository from the template, setting up the repository on your computer, and previewing the course website locally.

By the end of this chapter, the user has their own repository, can edit it locally, preview it, and publish their first change.

You do not need to be familiar with Git, GitHub, or Quarto to get started. The steps below explain which actions to take and where to find the relevant settings.

## Create accounts 


## Create a repository from the template

The first step is to create an independent copy of the SciLifeLab Course Webpage Template for your own course. Changes you make in your new repository will not affect the original template.

### Open the template repository

In your web browser, open the [SciLifeLab Course Webpage Template](https://github.com/SciLifeLab-Training/scilifelab-training-template-staging/tree/main).

Click the green **Use this template button** on the top right. Select **Create a new repository**.

<span style="color: red; font-weight: bold;">image:  fig-alt="GitHub repository page showing the Use this template button."</span>


### Configure your new repository

GitHub will open the **Create a new repository** page.

1. At the top, make sure to set `Include all branches` to **on** 

2. Under **Owner**, select the GitHub organisation or account where the course repository should be hosted (e.g. SciLifeLabDataCentre, SciLifeLab-Training, NBISweden, stockholmuniversity, or your personal account).

::: {.callout-note}
To create a repository within a GitHub organisation account, you need to be a member of the organisation account and have permission to create repositories. If the organisation you need does not appear under **Owner**, contact an administrator or owner of that organisation account.
:::

2. Under **Repository name**, enter a name for your course repository. Use lowercase letters where possible and use hyphens (`-`) instead of spaces, for example `introduction-to-r`.

::: {.callout-tip}
Choose the repository name carefully. The repository name becomes part of the URL of your published course website.
:::

3. Optionally, add a short description of the course.

5. Choose the repository **visibility**. For a course website containing training materials that should be openly accessible, select **Public**. Only select **Private** if access to the repository and course materials needs to be restricted.

6. Click `Create repository`

<span style="color: red; font-weight: bold;">image: fig-alt="GitHub form for creating a repository from a template, including the owner, repository name, visibility and Include all branches options.</span>

### Check your new repository

GitHub will create the repository and take you to its main page.

Check the repository name at the top of the page to make sure you are now working in **your new course repository**, rather than the original SciLifeLab Course Page Template repository.

<span style="color: red; font-weight: bold;"> image: fig-alt="GitHub page showing a newly created repository based on the course page template."</span>


### Add collaborators

If other people will help develop or maintain the course, you can give them access to the repository.

You can also return to this step later if you do not yet know who will contribute to the course.

1. In your course repository, select **Settings** in the repository navigation bar.

Under **Access** in the menu on the left, select **Collaborators and teams**.

<span style="color: red; font-weight: bold;">fig-alt="GitHub repository settings with Collaborators and teams selected under Access."</span>


2. Select **Add people** or **Add teams**, depending on who you want to give access to.

- Search for the GitHub user or team you want to add.
- Select the appropriate repository role.
- Confirm that you want to add the person or team.

::: {.callout-note}
The options available under **Collaborators and teams** depend on whether the repository belongs to a personal GitHub account or a GitHub organisation, and on your permissions within that organisation.
:::



## Clone the repository to your computer

You now have your course repository on GitHub. The next step is to create a copy of the repository on your computer so that you can edit, preview, and test the course website locally.

Creating a local copy of a GitHub repository is called **cloning**.

Changes you make to this local copy remain on your computer until you **commit** and **push** them back to GitHub. This allows you to experiment, preview your changes, and fix any mistakes before they become visible to collaborators or visitors to your course website.

### Copy the repository URL

On the main page of your course repository, click the green **Code** button.

Make sure **HTTPS** is selected, then copy the repository URL.

<span style="color: red; font-weight: bold;">Screenshot: GitHub Code menu showing the HTTPS repository URL.</span>

### Choose where to store the repository

Decide where you would like to keep your GitHub repositories on your computer. A common choice is to create a folder called `GitHub` inside your `Documents` folder.

To clone the repository into this location, you will use the terminal.

1. Open a terminal and navigate to the folder where you want to store your GitHub repositories.

For example, to use a `GitHub` folder inside `Documents` on macOS:

```bash
cd ~/Documents/GitHub
```

<span style="color: red; font-weight: bold;">Screenshot: Terminal showing the command above.</span>

::: {.callout-tip}
You only need to choose this location once. When you clone the repository, Git will automatically create a new folder with the repository name inside this location.
:::


2. After thism you will clone the repository. In your terminal,  run: 

```bash
git clone REPOSITORY-URL
```

Replace `REPOSITORY-URL` with the HTTPS URL you copied from GitHub.

For example:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/ORGANISATION/my-course.git
```

<span style="color: red; font-weight: bold;">Screenshot: Terminal showing the completed `git clone` command.</span>

Git will create a new folder containing your course repository.


## Open the repository in VS Code

Open **Visual Studio Code** and select:

**File → Open Folder...**

Navigate to the repository you just cloned and select the repository folder.

<span style="color: red; font-weight: bold;">Screenshot: VS Code showing the Open Folder dialog with the cloned repository selected.</span>

The repository files and folders should now appear in the **Explorer** panel on the left. You are now ready to set up the local environment you need to edit and preview your course website locally.


## Set up the local environment

Before previewing the course website, set up the Python environment and install the dependencies used by the template.

In VS Code, open a terminal using:

**Terminal → New Terminal**

The terminal should open in the root directory of your course repository.


### 1. Create a virtual environment

Run:

```bash
python3 -m venv .venv
```

This creates a Python virtual environment specifically for this repository.


### 2. Activate the virtual environment

On macOS or Linux, run:

```bash
source .venv/bin/activate
```

When the environment is active, you should see `(.venv)` at the beginning of the terminal prompt.

For example:

```text
(.venv) username@computer my-course %
```


### 3. Install the required dependencies

Run:

```bash
python -m pip install --upgrade pip
python -m pip install -r requirements-dev.txt
```

This installs the Python packages needed to generate, validate, and work on the course website.


## Preview the landing page 
localhost
automatic reloading
Ctrl+C
second terminal


You can now preview the landing page on your computer.

Run:

```bash
quarto preview
```

Quarto will render the website and start a local preview server. The terminal will display an address similar to:

```text
http://localhost:XXXX/
```

Open this address in your web browser if the preview does not open automatically.

![The SciLifeLab Course Page Template running as a local preview.](images/getting-started-local-preview.png){width=85% fig-align="center" fig-alt="Course landing page displayed locally in a web browser using Quarto preview."}

You are now viewing a local version of the course website. Changes you make to the landing-page files can be checked here before you publish them to GitHub.

::: {.callout-tip}
While `quarto preview` is running, the terminal is being used by the preview server. If you need to run other commands without stopping the preview, open a **second terminal** in VS Code.

To stop the preview server, return to the terminal in which it is running and press **Ctrl+C**.
:::
